title: compare
description: Two to four options side by side on the same criteria, the recommended one outlined in ink, and what decided it in one sentence; the weights can be the person’s own.

name.description: The option as people say it: “Sony XM6”, “DigitalOcean Droplet”, “Apartment in Gowanus”. The column header in the grid, the card title on cards.

image.description: A product shot or photo. Grid: a 44 pt thumbnail above the name, drawn only when every option has one. Cards: the top of the card. Fetched by the gateway like every remote image.

price.description: The headline price: large under the name on cards, and in the fallback. The grid shows price only as a criterion (so it can carry a weight); repeat it there when it should be a row.

pros.description: Up to four plus points, a few words each: “40 h battery”, “Folds flat”. Drawn on cards after a plus glyph.

cons.description: Up to four minus points: “Plasticky”, “24 h battery”. Drawn on cards after a minus glyph (shape, never colour alone).

url.description: The product or listing page, opened from the link glyph after the name (the domain shows first).

options.description: The options, in the order the agent ranks them or the order the person named them. 2–4.

label.description: What is compared: Price, Battery, Noise cancelling, Commute to work.

anyOf.description: A word when the value is a judgement: “Best”, “Very good”, “Yes”.

values.description: The value for each option, keyed by option id: a Quantity (formatted by the client, tabular figures) or a word. Every option needs a key; an unknown value is `{"value": null}` (shown as —, read as “unknown”), never a guess.

best.description: The options that win on this criterion. Their value is semibold and read as “best”. Omit when nothing stands out or it is a matter of taste.

weight.description: How much the criterion counts, 0–5 (0: shown, not counted). Needs `scores`. With `adjustable`, the starting value of the stepper.

scores.description: A score from 1 to 5 for each option on this criterion (5 is best), keyed by option id. Needs `weight`. The client needs a score for every option; an option the agent can’t score means the criterion gets no weight.

evidence.description: How the values are known: “rtings.com battery test, Sept 2026”. A caption under the label with a small glyph; a `claim` (“Sony says 40 h”) reads “Said by …”.

items.description: One row of the comparison: the same question asked of every option.

criteria.description: The rows, most important first. Optional only for a cards comparison where every option has pros or cons.

pick.description: The recommended option’s id: outlined in ink with a Pick badge. Omit when there is no clear winner (nothing is outlined). With `adjustable`, it must be the option with the highest weighted score at the sent weights.

decided_by.description: One sentence on what decided it, written to follow the option’s name and a colon (the client puts the name in front, in bold): “the same noise cancelling for less, with twice the battery. Battery decided it.” Required with `pick`; without one, what the choice hinges on, as a full sentence.

layout.description: auto: the grid on the iPhone column; cards on a wide column (≥ 560 pt) when every option has pros or cons, else the grid. `adjustable` always draws the grid.

adjustable.description: The person can change each criterion’s weight on the device (0–5). Scores re-rank locally, the outline and the Go with button follow the top score, and Reset Weights restores the sent weights. Needs at least one criterion with `weight` and `scores`.

choose.description: Show Go with <the top option> as the primary button. It sends `answer`. Use when the agent will act on the choice (book it, order it, draft the purchase for approval).
